title: Power Automate process mining: custom KPIs in the process intelligence experience
summary: Hold: the ownership API entry is an incomplete request, omitting the versioned Dataverse route and the body that identifies the new owner. The roadmap facts, ownership UI path and platform licensing statements are supported; the cited Learn pages opened successfully despite the pre-check's rate-limit responses.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Ownership reassignment is reached in Power Platform admin center through environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Users > user > Reassign records.
claims.quote: Select the environment where the process is located. ... select Settings. Under Users + permissions, select Users. Select the leaving user. On the command bar, select Reassign records.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: PATCH /msdyn_pminferredtasks(<msdyn_pminferredtaskid>) to update the ownerid property is the ownership reassignment call an administrator can use as printed.
claims.quote: Update operations use the HTTP PATCH verb. Pass a JSON object containing the properties you want to update to the URI that represents the record. ... PATCH [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/accounts(00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001) HTTP/1.1
claims.fix: Replace the incomplete call, including its rendered table copy, with 'PATCH <organization-uri>/api/data/v9.2/msdyn_pminferredtasks(<msdyn_pminferredtaskid>)' and specify Content-Type: application/json and the request body {"ownerid@odata.bind":"systemusers(<new-owner-systemuserid>)"}. The versioned entity path and ownerid navigation property are documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/reference/msdyn_pminferredtask; binding syntax is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/associate-disassociate-entities-using-web-api. Cite these alongside the existing table reference. Remove 'to update the ownerid property' from the executable call and retain it only as explanation.
